mutant.description: FOUR ARMS, because a one-arm guard proof cannot separate 'it catches the hazard' from 'it refuses everything' from 'the remedy it names is unreachable'. (1) POSITIVE: the opal_conservative_growth specimen planted as a model-class member. (2) NEGATIVE: the unchanged population re-run through the same function. (3) ESCAPE-ACCEPTED: the specimen plus a CROSSWALK_IDENTITY_MAP row naming a REAL crosswalk key ('opal_blend_5050_int_ltc') -- this tests that the remedy the error message TELLS the operator to use is one the guard actually honours. (4) ESCAPE-SHUT: the same specimen plus a row naming a BOGUS crosswalk key ('not_a_real_key') -- this tests that the escape cannot be used to launder an unknown member in.
mutant.expected: (1) RegistryError. (2) no raise. (3) no raise. (4) RegistryError.
mutant.observed: (1) RAISED RegistryError naming the id, the 11-key keyspace and both remedies. (2) no raise. (3) no raise -- the named remedy IS accepted. (4) RAISED -- a bogus crosswalk key cannot launder a member in. 4 of 4 arms behaved as expected. Arms 3 and 4 are the pair that matters: they differ in ONE field of ONE row (the crosswalk_model_key's membership in the keyspace) and produce OPPOSITE verdicts, so the guard is discriminating on that field and not on the row's mere presence.
